title: Benchmark matrix and acceptance thresholds (Runtime hardware tuning profiles pack)
author: Rina Kobayashi
content:
## Purpose
This page defines the **benchmark matrix** and **pass/fail acceptance thresholds** used to validate:
- New or modified **hardware tuning profiles** (kernel + scheduling + memory/KV cache knobs)
- New GPU SKUs entering the fleet (e.g., **B200** early access)
- Runtime releases where profile pack defaults or selection logic change

The goal is to prevent:
- **Tail latency regressions** (especially p99 under mixed workloads)
- **Stability regressions** (OOMs, allocator fragmentation, kernel fallbacks)
- Silent drift across heterogeneous fleet baselines (driver/CUDA differences)

This matrix is implemented in **benchmark-lab** and is referenced by CI/perf-canary gating.

---

## Scope and what this covers
### In scope
- Text generation (chat/completions), streaming on/off
- Prefill vs decode behavior, mixed prompt lengths
- Concurrency and queueing behavior (scheduler/backpressure)
- KV cache sizing, compaction behavior, memory headroom
- Kernel selection and fallback rates

### Out of scope
- Customer prompt sets/evals (covered by Applied ML evaluation harness)
- Full end-to-end product workflows (covered by application perf tests)

---

## Definitions (metrics)
We standardize on the following metrics, exported per run with tags: `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `sku`, `cuda_version`, `driver_version`, `model`, `quantization`, `workload_bucket`, `concurrency`.

### Latency
- **TTFT (ms)**: time to first token (streaming) / time to first output chunk.
- **TPOT (ms/token)**: time per output token during decode (steady-state).
- **E2E latency (ms)**: end-to-end request time (non-streaming).
- Percentiles reported: **p50 / p95 / p99**.

### Throughput
- **Output tokens/sec/GPU** (aggregate and per-request).
- **Requests/sec** (where applicable; mostly used for short decode buckets).

### Queueing / scheduler
- **scheduler_queue_ms** p50/p95/p99
- **admission_reject_rate** (if profile-aware admission control is enabled)
- **prefill_deprioritized_rate** (fraction of time prefill is delayed due to decode pressure; expected to be low outside mixed workloads)

### Kernel/runtime health
- **kernel_fallback_rate** (fraction of attention ops falling back from preferred kernel variant)
- **kernel_choice** distribution (e.g., H100 attention v3 vs fallback)
- **cuda_graph_replay_rate** (if enabled)

### Memory/KV cache
- **peak_gpu_mem_gb**, **steady_state_gpu_mem_gb**
- **kv_cache_reserved_gb** and **kv_cache_utilization**
- **oom_count** and **oom_rate**
- **allocator_fragmentation_est** (unitless estimate; see observability spec)
- **kv_compaction_count** and **kv_compaction_ms** p95

### Error metrics
- **request_error_rate** (5xx + timeouts)
- **timeout_rate** (client-side and server-side timeouts tracked separately)

---

## Benchmark environment requirements
To keep comparisons meaningful, benchmark-lab runs must record and (when gating) enforce:
- Runtime build: git SHA + runtime version (e.g., `runtime-1.22.x`)
- Profile pack version + active profile id
- GPU SKU and form factor (PCIe vs SXM if applicable)
- Driver/CUDA versions (exact)
- CPU model, NUMA config, hugepages status (if applicable)
- Container image digest

### Recommended baselines (used for lab standardization)
These are the lab “golden” environments; fleet can be more heterogeneous, but gating uses the lab.
- **H100**: CUDA 12.4.x + driver 550.xx (golden); no MIG
- **L40S**: CUDA 12.3.x + driver 545.xx (golden)
- **B200 (preview)**: CUDA 12.4/12.5 + driver 555.xx (see B200 bring-up notes; gating is more conservative)

If a run deviates from the golden environment, results are still captured but not used for merge-blocking gates unless explicitly approved by Runtime + SRE.

---

## Model set (representative serving models)
We maintain a small, stable set for gating and a larger “extended set” for nightly coverage.

### Gating set (merge-blocking)
1. **Llama 3.1 8B Instruct** (FP16/BF16)
2. **Llama 3.1 70B Instruct** (BF16; tensor-parallel as per SKU)
3. **Qwen2.5 7B Instruct** (BF16)
4. **Mixtral 8x7B Instruct** (BF16; exercises routing + MoE-ish compute patterns)

### Extended set (nightly, non-blocking by default)
- **Qwen2.5 72B Instruct** (BF16)
- **Llama 3.1 8B Instruct** (INT8 weight-only / quant profile used by Optimize)
- One long-context model variant (when enabled in catalog) to stress KV + kernel fallbacks

Notes:
- Quantized runs are included because some kernel/scheduler knobs interact with sequence-length distributions and memory headroom.
- Model versions are pinned by immutable artifact digest in benchmark-lab.

---

## Workload buckets
Buckets are designed to capture the most common production shapes while keeping runtime manageable.

### Token shape buckets
All token counts refer to **post-tokenization** lengths.

| Bucket ID | Prompt tokens (prefill) | Output tokens (decode) | Primary risk | Typical product usage |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| S1 | 64–256 | 32–128 | scheduler overhead, TTFT | autocomplete, short Q&A |
| S2 | 256–1,024 | 128–512 | batching vs latency | chat, agents |
| M1 | 1,024–4,096 | 128–512 | prefill pressure, queueing | retrieval + chat |
| M2 | 1,024–4,096 | 512–1,536 | decode efficiency, tail | long answers |
| L1 | 4,096–8,192 | 128–512 | KV headroom, kernel fallback | long context chat |
| L2 | 4,096–8,192 | 512–2,048 | OOM/fragmentation, p99 | summarization, analysis |

### Mixed-workload bucket (tail latency stress)
**MX** is a mixture designed to reproduce real Hosted/Dedicated traffic:
- 50% S2, 30% M1, 15% M2, 5% L1
- Prompts and outputs are sampled from distributions (see below)
- Concurrency includes burst phases to test backpressure

---

## Prompt/response length distributions
For each bucket, benchmark-lab samples from a distribution (not a single fixed length) to avoid overfitting to one sequence length.

### Distributions
- Prompt tokens: log-uniform within bucket range (bias toward lower end, matching prod)
- Output tokens: truncated geometric within bucket range (bias toward shorter outputs)

### Seeds and run length
- Each (model, bucket, concurrency) run uses **3 seeds**.
- Minimum run duration: **12 minutes** (2 min warmup + 10 min measured).
- For MX bucket: **20 minutes** (captures burst behavior).

---

## Concurrency levels (per SKU)
Concurrency is expressed as in-flight requests per GPU (or per model replica when sharded). Values below are targets; profile admission control may cap actual concurrency.

| SKU | Concurrency set | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| H100 | 1, 4, 8, 16 | exercises batching, queueing, and decode saturation |
| L40S | 1, 2, 4, 8 | stability-first; higher conc often drives OOM/fragmentation under long context |
| B200 (preview) | 1, 4, 8, 16 | expected to behave like/above H100, but gating is conservative until fleet baselines stabilize |

For large models (70B/72B), “per GPU concurrency” is computed as `in_flight_requests / num_gpus_in_replica` and reported both ways.

---

## Benchmark matrix (what runs are required)
### Merge-blocking matrix (required for profile pack changes)
A change is considered “profile-impacting” if it touches:
- profile defaults (scheduler/batching/KV/memory)
- kernel selection rules
- compatibility/selection logic
- admission control logic

Required runs:
1) **H100**
- Models: 8B + 70B
- Buckets: S2, M1, M2, L1, MX
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 16 (S2/M1/M2), and 1, 4, 8 (L1/MX)

2) **L40S**
- Models: 8B (and 70B if supported in L40S lab pool)
- Buckets: S2, M1, M2, L1, MX
- Concurrency: 1, 4, 8 (S2/M1/M2) and 1, 2, 4 (L1/MX)

3) **B200 (preview)**
- Models: 8B
- Buckets: S2, M1, MX
- Concurrency: 1, 8
- Status: allowed-to-fail until B200 driver baseline is standardized; failures must be triaged and tracked.

### Nightly matrix (non-blocking, broader coverage)
- Add remaining buckets (S1, L2)
- Add extended model set (quantized, 72B)
- Add streaming on/off variants

---

## Acceptance thresholds
Thresholds are evaluated against a **baseline**:
- Baseline is the latest green run on the same golden environment for the target branch (typically `main`) with the previous profile pack version.
- Comparisons are done per (sku, model, bucket, concurrency).

### Global hard-fail thresholds (all SKUs)
A run is an automatic **FAIL** if any of the following occur in measured window:
- **request_error_rate > 0.20%** (excluding known injected failures)
- **timeout_rate > 0.10%**
- **oom_count > 0** on any gating run
- **kernel_fallback_rate increases by > 2.0 percentage points** vs baseline AND p95 latency also regresses (indicates true fallback regression, not just noise)
- **scheduler_queue_ms p99 increases by > 25%** vs baseline on MX (queueing regression)

### H100 acceptance thresholds
H100 is our primary Hosted/Dedicated performance anchor. We optimize for **tail latency stability** without sacrificing sustained throughput.

**Latency gates (H100):**
- S2/M1/M2:
  - TTFT p95: **no worse than +7%** vs baseline
  - TPOT p95: **no worse than +5%** vs baseline
  - E2E p99 (non-streaming variant in nightly): **no worse than +8%**
- L1:
  - TTFT p95: **no worse than +10%** (prefill sensitivity acknowledged)
  - TPOT p95: **no worse than +6%**
- MX:
  - TTFT p99: **no worse than +8%**
  - scheduler_queue_ms p99: **no worse than +15%**

**Throughput gates (H100):**
- Output tokens/sec/GPU (aggregate): **no worse than -4%** vs baseline on S2/M1/M2 at high concurrency.

**Memory/KV gates (H100):**
- peak_gpu_mem_gb: **no worse than +3%** vs baseline on L1/MX (prevents headroom erosion)
- allocator_fragmentation_est: **no worse than +0.05 absolute** on L1/MX (if metric is available; otherwise informational)

### L40S acceptance thresholds
L40S is stability-sensitive. We bias toward conservative memory headroom and avoid long-context-induced instability.

**Latency gates (L40S):**
- S2/M1/M2:
  - TTFT p95: **no worse than +10%** vs baseline
  - TPOT p95: **no worse than +7%** vs baseline
- L1:
  - TTFT p95: **no worse than +12%** vs baseline
  - TPOT p95: **no worse than +8%** vs baseline
- MX:
  - TTFT p99: **no worse than +10%** vs baseline
  - scheduler_queue_ms p99: **no worse than +20%** vs baseline

**Throughput gates (L40S):**
- Output tokens/sec/GPU (aggregate): **no worse than -6%** vs baseline at top tested concurrency.

**Memory/KV gates (L40S):**
- Strict: **oom_count must be 0**
- peak_gpu_mem_gb: **no worse than +2%** vs baseline on L1/MX
- kv_compaction_ms p95: **no worse than +15%** vs baseline (compaction regressions often show up as long-tail latency)

### B200 (preview) acceptance thresholds
B200 validation is split into two modes:
- **Bring-up mode (default until fleet baseline is stable):** only hard-fail thresholds apply; performance deltas are reported but do not block merges.
- **Gating mode (explicitly enabled per release train):** relative thresholds apply.

**Bring-up mode expectations (report-only):**
- kernel_fallback_rate should be **<= 1%** on S2/M1; if >1%, file a Runtime issue tagged `b200-kernels`.
- TTFT/TPOT should be within **±15%** of H100 normalized expectation (informational; not merge-blocking).

**Gating mode thresholds (when enabled):**
- TTFT p95: **no worse than +8%** vs B200 baseline
- TPOT p95: **no worse than +6%** vs B200 baseline
- Output tokens/sec/GPU: **no worse than -5%** vs B200 baseline
- peak_gpu_mem_gb: **no worse than +3%** vs B200 baseline

---

## Pass/Fail rules and triage notes
### How we decide PASS vs FAIL
A change is **PASS** if:
- All global hard-fail thresholds pass
- All SKU-specific relative thresholds pass for the merge-blocking matrix

A change is **SOFT FAIL** (requires sign-off) if:
- Only throughput regresses (within 2–6% band) but latency improves significantly, OR
- A regression is isolated to one model/bucket and is explainable by an intended knob change with documented trade-off

A change is **FAIL** if:
- Any hard-fail triggers
- Any latency tail (p99) regression over threshold in MX, unless explicitly waived by Runtime + SRE for a time-bound experiment

### Noise handling
Benchmark-lab uses 3 seeds; we consider a regression “real” if at least **2/3 seeds** exceed the threshold in the same direction.

If results are noisy:
- Re-run the exact failing tuple (same seed list).
- If still noisy, check:
  - GPU clock / throttling
  - background jobs on the node
  - driver mismatch vs golden

---

## Data capture and artifacts
Every run must publish:
- Raw per-request samples (anonymized synthetic prompts)
- Aggregated percentile summary
- Runtime metrics snapshot (Prometheus scrape export)
- Active profile summary (resolved knob values)

Artifact tags:
- `profile_version`, `profile_id`, `sku`, `model`, `bucket`, `concurrency`, `git_sha`

Retention:
- Merge-blocking artifacts: 90 days
- Nightly artifacts: 30 days
- Release candidate runs: 180 days

---

## Operational linkage (SRE rollout gates)
These benchmark thresholds are designed to line up with rollout SLO guardrails:
- MX bucket TTFT p99 and scheduler_queue_ms p99 are the closest lab analogs to production tail behavior under mixed workloads.

If a change barely passes lab but regresses production, we will:
1) add/adjust MX mixture weights or concurrency
2) add a targeted bucket (e.g., longer prefill bursts)
3) tighten per-SKU thresholds

---

## Change management
Any modifications to:
- Gating model set
- Bucket definitions or distributions
- Threshold percentages

…must be documented in a short changelog section at the bottom of this page and referenced in the runtime release note.

### Changelog
- 2026-02-19: Updated MX acceptance criteria to include scheduler_queue_ms p99 deltas; added kv_compaction_ms p95 gate on L40S.
- 2026-02-10: Added B200 bring-up mode expectations and allowed-to-fail policy for initial smoke suite.
- 2026-01-27: Defined initial H100/L40S relative thresholds and standardized 3-seed minimum for gating runs.
